page: Microsoft Azure L24aos_v4 is a storage-focused and memory-optimized server instance belonging to the Laosv4 family. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The configuration provides 24 vCPUs across 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It features 192.0 GB of RAM, translating to 8.0 GB of memory per core. A key hardware highlight is the inclusion of 17,279 GB of local storage, with Premium Storage capability supported under Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance is also robust, with Geekbench multi-core scores ranking in the top 25%, though stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores fall within the average tier. Memory bandwidth and database operations, including Redis SET operations, consistently perform in the average range. For specialized workloads, the instance demonstrates top-tier performance in text generation for small language models, though performance drops to the bottom 25% when processing prompts on large 70B models due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the L24aos_v4 offers high resource density, combining substantial memory capacity with an exceptionally large local storage allocation. This makes it highly suitable for data-intensive workloads that require rapid access to large local datasets without the overhead of external storage. Recommended workloads include large-scale databases, data warehousing, big data analytics, and memory-intensive applications. However, for large-scale AI model inference or heavy parallel computing, the lack of a GPU and the average multi-core scaling present clear tradeoffs.
